item.title: August job numbers far exceed economists' expectations
item.description: Employers added 162,000 jobs in August, according to the Labor Department on Friday. Economists had expected the labor market to add about 53,000 jobs.
item.content:encoded: Employers added 162,000 jobs in August, according to the Labor Department on Friday. Economists had expected the labor market to add about 53,000 jobs.
item.dc:creator: Scott Horsley

item.title: Why the U.S. Treasury is buying back double the government bonds it normally does
item.description: The U.S. Treasury is planning to buy back at least double the long-dated government bonds it usually does. Will the plan pit the Treasury secretary against both the bond markets and the Fed?
item.content:encoded: The U.S. Treasury is planning to buy back at least double the long-dated government bonds it usually does. Will the plan pit the Treasury secretary against both the bond markets and the Fed?

item.title: What's up with the bond market?
item.description: NPR's Scott Detrow talks with economist Justin Wolfers of the University of Michigan about what's going on with the bond market — and why it matters to everyday people.

item.title: The IRS slashed its staff. One result? More taxes going uncollected
item.description: The IRS slashed its auditing staff last year — but the move may have backfired as tax collections from enforcement efforts plummeted, an Inspector General report shows.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Trump says U.S. has struck a deal for control of Venezuelan oil reserves
item.description: President Trump says a new deal with Venezuela would give the U.S. control of more than 65 billion barrels of oil reserves.

item.title: Global trade expert Wendy Cutler explores U.S. trade wars with Canada and Iran
item.description: The trade war escalated between the U.S. and Canada, and the Trump administration tried to cut off Iran economically. NPR's Scott Simon talks with Wendy Cutler of the Asia Society Policy Institute.

item.title: Fed's Kevin Warsh warns inflation is too high, sparking bets rate hikes are coming
item.description: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated his commitment to fighting inflation in a major speech — raising expectations that rate hikes may be coming, though he did not clearly spell out a path going forward.

item.title: U.S. says pipelines will make Strait of Hormuz irrelevant. Energy experts disagree
item.description: Treasure Secretary Scott Bessent said oil pipelines will make Strait of Hormuz irrelevant in two years. Energy experts say that is unlikely to happen.
